text_pending_judge.text: Amazon's FY2025 10-K says the results of operations of its international stores and product and service offerings, and certain intercompany balances, are exposed to foreign exchange rate fluctuations. It adds that as it has expanded internationally, its exposure to exchange rate fluctuations has increased.
Amazon says its reporting currency is the U.S. Dollar and that changes in foreign exchange rates significantly affect its reported results and consolidated trends.
Amazon reported that FX fluctuations during the year, compared with prior-year rates, increased International segment net sales by $4.9 billion in FY2025.

Based on foreign funds of $29.7 billion at December 31, 2025, Amazon says an assumed 5%, 10% and 20% adverse change in foreign exchange would reduce them by $1.5 billion, $3.0 billion and $5.9 billion respectively.

Amazon's FY2025 10-K says the results of operations of its international stores and product and service offerings, and certain intercompany balances, are exposed to foreign exchange rate fluctuations. It adds that as it has expanded internationally, its exposure to exchange rate fluctuations has increased.
Item 7A states that the results of operations of, and certain intercompany balances associated with, Amazon's internationally-focused stores and AWS are exposed to foreign exchange rate fluctuations.
Amazon says its reporting currency is the U.S. Dollar and that changes in foreign exchange rates significantly affect its reported results and consolidated trends.
Amazon says that when the U.S. Dollar strengthens against the currencies in which it holds cash equivalents and marketable securities, those balances, when translated, may be materially less than expected, and vice versa.
Amazon reported that FX fluctuations during the year, compared with prior-year rates, increased International segment net sales by $4.9 billion in FY2025.
Based on foreign funds of $29.7 billion at December 31, 2025, Amazon says an assumed 5%, 10% and 20% adverse change in foreign exchange would reduce them by $1.5 billion, $3.0 billion and $5.9 billion respectively.
Amazon's risk factors list limitations on the repatriation and investment of funds and foreign currency exchange restrictions among its international operating risks. They also cite changes in foreign exchange rates as one factor affecting its tax expense and liabilities.
In the Q2 2026 10-Q, Amazon said FX changes did not significantly affect net sales for Q2 2026 but increased net sales by $3.0 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Of that, International net sales rose by $2.4 billion and North America net sales by $485 million.
Amazon's Q3 2026 guidance language says its results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors, such as fluctuations in foreign exchange rates and energy prices.
